issues.failure_explanation: The volume term must be linear in the first argument, \phih; as written it contains \wh twice. Thus the defined functional is not the advective bilinear form used later, and an off-diagonal call such as \bupwind(\bfv;\eIu,\ehu) does not contain \eIu in the volume term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first \wh in the volume term by \phih and use the resulting bilinear form consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The off-diagonal upwind estimate and the concentration convergence proof that invokes it are unreliable as written.
issues.title: Upwind form uses the test function twice in the volume term
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single forced symbol replacement and preserves the dissipation identity, estimates, and rates.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating the mass term gives ((1+κp_h)p_{h,t})_t=(1+κp_h)p_{h,tt}+κp_{h,t}^2. The displayed right-hand side F therefore lacks the required factor κ in front of \pi_h((\qh)^2), so the Picard argument proves local existence for a different ODE when κ≠0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert κ immediately before \pi_h((\qh)^2) in the definition of F; the subsequent local Lipschitz, extension, and error arguments are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The local existence proposition does not establish existence for the stated discrete pressure problem, and the pressure well-posedness theorem and the coupled-model theorem inherit that gap.
issues.title: First-order pressure ODE omits the factor κ in the quadratic term
